candidate_sentences.text: The Group expanded its portfolio through the acquisition of 96.6% of Estonia Farmid and 100% of Oisu Biogaas, while continuing investments in biomethane, solar generation, battery storage and real estate.
These developments supported Infortar’s strategy of diversification and more stable cash flows.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K6, K7, and K8 are all adequately represented in the candidate summary with supporting sentences identified. K5 is missing entirely - there is no mention of the Rimi logistics centre, Depo DIY retail space, or the Rail Baltica construction contract. While the summary covers most high-importance material (revenue growth, drivers, segments, acquisitions, financials, and strategy), the omission of a specific major development project (K5) prevents a 'Yes' rating. The overall picture is captured but with a notable gap in a high-importance area.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support each other without contradictions. The summary follows a clear structure: starting with overall performance, then detailing revenue/EBITDA growth, explaining drivers of performance, discussing net profit decline due to one-off effects, segment performance, strategic developments, and concluding with financial position and cash flow. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues. While there is a significant net profit decline mentioned, it is clearly attributed to non-recurring effects in 2024 (S5, S6, S7), which is consistent with the reported growth in other metrics. The segment figures (S9, S10, S11) are presented as separate business lines without any claim that they should sum to consolidated totals, so no arithmetic contradictions arise. The summary avoids unnecessary repetition and maintains clarity throughout.
